brief: Client GS L/S fund performance fell -1.02% (9/11-9/17) vs +0.35% MSCI World, driven by long-side alpha losses, as breadth deteriorated: under 30% of S&P names sit above their 50-day average and the GS Sentiment Indicator hit -0.9, a one-year low, while AAII bearish sentiment jumped to 53.3%. Flows are not uniformly bearish though: EPFR shows $79.3bn into equities last week ($63.8bn US, fastest pace in three months), GS PB data shows the largest US net buying in five weeks, and hedge funds have net bought Software for four straight weeks, though allocation remains only in the 13th percentile over five years. GS argues the tape is not overextended: Q2 EPS grew 51% y/y while forward P/E compressed from 23x to 19x, supporting its 8,700 S&P target. The Fed's Warsh called the hike a removal of policy accommodation; GS economists now add an October hike but keep the terminal rate at 3.25-3.50%. Gold's end-2027 target holds at $5,400 even as near-term fair value is trimmed to $4,650 on rate pressure. GS also cites Meta's Muse app's 1.6mm US downloads in eight days and prefers long AI-agent-driven beneficiaries over consumer-inertia stocks AI could make less sticky.
